task_context.target_type: report.Renderer (declared across report/renderer.go, report/renderer_data.go, report/renderer_templates.go, report/renderer_reports.go)
task_context.injected_arrangement: One rendering type owns format dispatch, the suppressed-finding policy, the concrete serialization bodies of the json/yaml/csv/golint/html/text formats, byte assembly around the junit-xml/sonarqube builders, sarif wiring, the text color themes and template function map, code-snippet reconstruction and line-range parsing, the embedded templates in report/, and the CLI's finding-ordering helpers (report.OrderIssuesForReport / report.IssueLeadingLine wrapping). The six per-format packages (report/json, report/yaml, report/csv, report/golint, report/html, report/text) are reduced to forwarding shims into report.WriteJSON/WriteYAML/WriteCSV/WriteGolint/WriteHTML/WriteText; cmd/gosec's sortIssues and extractLineNumber delegate into the report package.
task_context.compatibility_boundary: Behavior and public API are locked: identical rendered bytes for all nine formats; report.CreateReport, per-format WriteReport entries (text keeps its enableColor parameter), junit.GenerateReport, sonar.GenerateReport and the report/sarif public surface unchanged; unknown or empty format names fall back to text rendering; suppressed findings appear only in json and sarif output.

rubrics.criterion: No single type combines format dispatch, the suppressed-finding policy, and the concrete rendering bodies of multiple output families: after the repair, each serialization family present before the change (whole-document marshal for json/yaml, record-oriented assembly for csv, line-oriented formatting for golint, template-driven rendering for text/html, byte assembly around the junit-xml/sonarqube builders) is implemented by format-specific code that does not share one receiver with the other families.
rubrics.rationale: The multi-format receiver is the core of this instance: the injected state implements every format as a method group on one type, so the resolution is measured by whether that receiver arrangement is actually dismantled, not by whether files were renamed.

rubrics.criterion: What is genuinely shared is a small explicit mechanism: selecting a renderer by format name (preserving the existing fallback to text rendering for unknown or empty names) and applying the suppressed-finding rule (suppressed findings are dropped for every format except json and sarif) live outside the per-format renderers, and the suppression rule is not re-implemented inside each per-format renderer.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt asks for dispatch and policy as an explicit mechanism rather than as property of the type that also implements the formats; duplicating the suppression predicate into every renderer or scattering the format-name switch would trade one defect for another.

rubrics.criterion: The text-family presentation mechanisms - the severity color themes, the text template function map including its enableColor behavior, code-snippet reconstruction, and issue line-range parsing - are owned by the text rendering code path rather than by a cross-format owner.
rubrics.rationale: These helpers were absorbed onto the central type even though only the text rendering uses them; returning them to their consumer is a location-specific obligation of this case that file moves alone do not discharge.

rubrics.criterion: The embedded template assets live in the directory of the package that embeds and renders them, and each asset is embedded exactly once.
rubrics.rationale: The two template files were relocated into the report package when rendering was centralized; go:embed ties an asset to its embedding package, so any sound redistribution must carry the assets along and must not strand a second copy elsewhere.

rubrics.criterion: The finding-ordering responsibility (the severity comparator and its leading-line extraction applied by the CLI before a report is printed or saved) has exactly one owner inside the reporting/CLI path, and no duplicate copy of the comparator remains in the report package or elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: Ordering was pulled into the central type as part of the consolidation; the repair must re-home it, and graders must verify there is one implementation, not two divergent ones.

rubrics.criterion: The repair redistributes every format without deleting behavior: all nine output formats still have a real implementation reachable from their format names, rather than one or more formats being stubbed, merged into another format's path, or dropped from dispatch.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible shortcut for this instance is to delete the large coordinator group and re-implement only the easy formats; the compatibility boundary in the prompt forbids it, so graders should check each format survived.

rubrics.criterion: Each of the six per-format writer packages (report/json, report/yaml, report/csv, report/golint, report/html, report/text) has its exported entry point backed by that format's owning code, not by a call into a cross-format type situated in the parent report package.
rubrics.rationale: The injection specifically gutted these packages into pass-throughs; restoring their format ownership is the coupled change without which the core resolution is cosmetic.

rubrics.criterion: The two irregular input flows keep flowing only to their consumers: enableColor affects only the text rendering, and the root paths passed by the CLI affect only the sarif report.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state carries these two parameters through a builder chain on the central type; a repair that removes the chain must re-route both parameters precisely, and this is where routing mistakes concentrate.

rubrics.criterion: The junit-xml and sonarqube render paths obtain their documents from the existing builder APIs with unchanged public signatures, with only byte-level assembly (marshal, indent, xml header, stream write) at the rendering call site, and the report/sarif public surface is not modified.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt carves these builder APIs out of scope; the repair must respect that boundary while still removing their assembly from any cross-format owner.

rubrics.criterion: The per-format packages do not remain pass-throughs into some replacement cross-format intermediary: the old forwarding pattern is not preserved under a new name (for example a new multi-format type or hub in another package that the format packages still merely call into).
rubrics.rationale: This is the specific way a solver can move files around while leaving the injected relation intact, so it is graded as a distinct failure of the coupled ownership restoration.

rubrics.criterion: The former coordination plumbing is fully removed: no orphaned factory, builder-stage, dispatch, or shared-emitter members of the dismantled owner linger as dead code, and none of report/renderer.go, report/renderer_data.go, report/renderer_templates.go, report/renderer_reports.go survives as a vestigial forwarding shell.
rubrics.rationale: The central type is spread over a four-file method group; a repair that dismantles the receiver but leaves the files or their now-unreferenced helpers behind has not cleaned up after itself.

rubrics.criterion: No stranded template assets remain: every template file in the repository is embedded by exactly one package, and directories whose packages no longer embed or render a template do not retain unreferenced copies.
rubrics.rationale: go:embed makes it easy to leave the old asset file behind after a move because nothing deletes it automatically; this instance moved both templates and requires the final tree to carry each asset once.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave unreachable duplicates of the absorbed helpers, such as a second copy of the code-snippet/line-range parsing family, an extra suppression predicate, or a duplicated comparator that no remaining code path uses.
rubrics.rationale: When re-homing logic out of a large method group, copy-then-forget is a realistic residue; graders should verify each absorbed helper has exactly one live implementation.

rubrics.criterion: No format renders different bytes for the same input: json still uses tab-indented marshaling and yaml its marshal layout, csv keeps its column order, per-issue row content, flush, and write-error propagation, golint keeps its line format and line-number computation, junit-xml keeps its xml header and indent, and the text/html/snippet rendering keeps the exact marker and indentation bytes.
rubrics.rationale: These formats are byte-locked by the repository's output tests; listing the concrete surfaces graders must compare keeps this item answerable from the solver patch and the suite rather than a generic request to avoid bugs.

rubrics.criterion: The suppressed-finding rule does not flip: suppressed findings still appear in json and sarif output and are still excluded from every other format.
rubrics.rationale: The policy rides the central data path in the injected state, so moving renderers is exactly where an accidental drop or leak of suppressed findings would originate in this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Dispatch and ordering behavior is preserved: an unknown or empty format name still falls back to the text rendering instead of erroring or producing empty output, and findings still come out severity-descending when sorting is enabled (its default), without being ordered twice or not at all.
rubrics.rationale: The fall-through in the format switch and the CLI ordering step were both centralization sites in this case and both have directly observable regressions; each is cheap to verify from the patch and tests.

rubrics.criterion: The exported reporting surface does not change: report.CreateReport keeps its current parameter list, every per-format WriteReport keeps its current signature and package (text keeps its enableColor parameter), and junit.GenerateReport, sonar.GenerateReport and the report/sarif public functions keep their names, signatures and locations.
rubrics.rationale: Library consumers import these exact entry points, and part of this task's difficulty is redistributing ownership across packages without moving the public surface, so graders must confirm signatures survived the reorganization.
